AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Incidences of sexual dysfunction due to the use of 5 α-reductase inhibitors have been suggested. Despite low sexual dysfunction reported in clinical trials, an analysis of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) database revealed a significant disproportionality in the reporting of sexual dysfunction with the use of finasteride. Therefore, it is likely that a similar relationship with dutasteride may exist.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To determine whether dutasteride use leads to a higher risk of sexual dysfunction compared to a baseline risk for all other drugs using the FAERS database.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: A case by non-case disproportionality approach was used whereby a reporting odds ratio (ROR) with 95% confidence interval (CI) was calculated. Cases of dutasteride-associated sexual dysfunction were compared to a reference risk of sexual dysfunction for all other drugs in the database.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: A significant disproportionality in reporting of sexual dysfunction with the use of dutasteride was observed. The disproportionality was present for all age ranges except for 31-45 years where there were few overall reports of adverse events.

AbstractText.Label: LIMITATIONS
AbstractText.content: Adverse events can be underreported, and selection bias is inherent in the FAERS.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Dutasteride use is associated with an increase in reports of sexual dysfunction.
